answer: An agent economy can tie rewards to funding provenance. The ledger traces where each key got its first coins and merges keys with a shared funding ancestor into one cluster that earns a single reward share regardless of size, while each key pays 10 POA upkeep per epoch. Every extra clone thus adds cost but no income. To escape, a farm must forge a separate history per key, paid by distinct counterparties for real work over several epochs, which no one sells in bulk. Mixers are no haven: mixed coins put a key on half-weight probation. A jade trader paid by its own clients is a cluster of one.
